body:
I would just like to get a few things off my chest and out in the marketplace of ideas about this troublesome and, I believe, dangerous compound.
In my opinion, the popularity of 5MEO-DiPT illustrates how significantly the power of suggestion and pre-conceived notions can effect the way one experiences psychedelics.
5MEO-DiPT has not been a widely available material for very long, being one of the later products to be offered by various gray market companies that sprang up in the mid to late 90s selling research chemicals. From the time it first started to become available on the gray market(circa 1999), the true nature of this chemical has been grossly distorted in a wide range of half truths and myths, usually suggesting that it is a close approximation of MDMA, 2CB or LSD.
The truth is this compound is far more likely to produce effects reminiscent of a few packages of morning glory seeds, complete with nausea and diarhea. It may also cause serious damage to the eyes, but more on that later.
A primary source of the myths about 5MEO-DiPT, as is so often the case, is 'TIHKAL' by Dr. Alexander Shulgin. Under the entry for 5MEO-DiPT, Shulgin writes:
'Here is a rather fast-acting psychedelic-like drug, with suggestions of LSD action but with essential differences. It has a lot of things going for it. It is short-lived, a virtue in many people's minds. It may vie with 2C-B as a potential aphrodisiac. It is reasonably easy to synthesize. It is of a pretty high potency. The physical side-effects are minimal. These are the positive points.' - Alexander Shulgin, 'TIHKAL'
Compare these comments with what he had to say in a more recent interview about this same substance:
Alexander Shulgin: Well, actually at the regular full dose -- 12 or 15 mg, I don't know how much you used -- it is not a terribly satisfactory psychedelic.
Interviewer: Right. I agree.
Alexander Shulgin: However, if you ever have a chance, try 6 mg.
Ann Shulgin: Now, for a young person, it may not be the same...
Alexander Shulgin: It may not be, okay. But 6 mg... it does not help erections one damn bit, at all; you're still on your own in that area. But if you get to the point of orgasm, it's explosive. It's almost scary! Small amounts intensify orgasm. Not for Ann, but for me. Is it a male/ female thing? I don't know.
[source: http://www.maps.org/news-letters/v12n1/12103shu.html]
No nearly as enthusiastic, is he?
In fairness to Dr. Shulgin, in the same TIHKAL entry he goes on to point out negatives reports about the effects of 'Foxy':
'But there are points that are neutral or actually negative, and they must be considered. A fair number of people who have explored 5-MeO-DIPT have said that there are some uncomfortable aspects with the experience. Not only are there few if any visual enhancements, but the altered state they entered was one that they simply couldn't use. They couldn't make intuitive leaps. That they were wasting their time. ' Alexander Shulgin, 'TIHKAL'
I don't think the fault lies so much with Dr. Shulgin as it does with the tendency of many readers of 'TIHKAL' (and 'PIHKAL' for that matter) to remember the positive descriptions and forget the negative or neutral ones.
Unfortunately, for many entheogen enthusiasts, the lasting impression of the TIHKAL entry on 'Foxy' was the suggestion that that there might be a legal and easily obtainable psychedelic that rivaled LSD, MDMA and 2CB in its effects. When many of these excited TIHKAL readers went on to spread the word about this then little known substance to fellow entheogen enthusiasts, they were far more likely to remember and describe the comparisons to 2CB and LSD than the fact that for many of Shulgin's tets subjects the drug was 'a waste of time.' And we all know how stories tend to get increasingly embellished and/or distorted the further they get from their original source.
Further complicating matters is the fact that the effects of psychedelics are so variable and so susceptible to the influence of pre-conceived notions of a drug's effects that many people who actually acquired and tried the substance reported experience effects comparable to MDMA, 2CB or some other entheogenic superpower. The idea that there was something 'special' about 5MEO-DiPT was further fueled when it acquired its popular and suggestive nickname-'Foxy'. Nothing popularizes a drug faster than a catchy, suggestive nickname.
Eventually, less enthusiastic and sometimes downright scary reports of the drugs effects started to make their way around the entheogenic community, ranging from simple realizations that there is nothing particularly 'special' about 'Foxy' to reports of emergency room overdoses, violent outbursts and catastrophic encounters with police. It has recently been emergency scheduled as a Level I controlled substance by the DEA, meaning it is now as illegal as heroin or cocaine.
I would like to do my part to clear up some of the misconceptions and dangerous hype about 5MEO-DiPT that have been spreading like wild fire for several years now.
I experimented with 5MEO-DiPT perhaps a dozen times in the year 2000, with doses in the 5 to 20 mg range. I know the substance and its effects well.
For one thing, there is virtually no visual activity with the substance. Mild to moderate nausea and diarhea frequently occur during the first hour after ingestion, comparable to but generally not as bad or annoying as one might experience after eating, say, 150 morning glory seeds.
Rather than any sort of 2CB-ish body high, it simply produces a sense of muscular rigidity or tenseness. It seems to effect circulation in some sense, as the hands often feel cold and stiff while under the influence of this substance. It does not inspire much in the way of introspection, and is in fact a rather subduing and 'stoning' or stupifying high. You feel doped up. In short, I found to be a good approximation of a bad morning glory seed high.
In fact, its effects are so singularly uninspiring that I ended up throwing away approximately 400 milligrams of the substance, having no interest in it myself and not being able to find anyone among my friends who had experimented with the material that was interested in doing more.
There is one effect of 5MEO-DiPT that I have not yet mentioned, and this is perhaps the most ominous aspect of this troublesome compound. Myself and several of my friends had noticed when we had taken 5MEO-DiPT either outdoors or in a well lit area that we could see 'floaters' in our field of vision. These were easily not psychedelic visuals or distortions of any kind, and in fact would often be apparent BEFORE any actual intoxication set in. We all reported seeing dark spots and cobweb like strands floating in the field of vision. One friend described it as looking like 'mud on a car windshield'. Another described it as having the apearance of black dye dissipating in water. Most ominously was a friend who said 'this isn't good' and speculated that it indicated a rupture of the retina.
This floater effect always went away by the time the drug wore off and we thought little of it until about a year ago, when slowly, over the course of the past year, nearly every one of my friends who had experimented with the substance- including one who only did it once (the guy who made the ominous comment about the retina rupturing) started to experience chronic floaters in BOTH eyes.
While chronic floaters are common in people over 60, they are virtually unheard of among people under 30, such as myself and my friends.
I went to see an eye doctor, and he confirmed that there were three small retinal holes in one eye and one in the other.
When I saw recently that an Anonymous poster to Erowid reported experiencing a 'lasting spot in the eye' after using 5MEO-DiPT, I knew I had to tell my story.
Instead of 'Foxy', why not call it 'Eye Fuck'.
